items.text: California Governor Newsom signed a law making it a crime to seize voted ballots, prompted by a county sheriff's seizure of 650,000 ballots ahead of the June 2 primary
New Mexico court ordered Republican Party chair Amy Barela to step down ahead of the June 2 primary, ruling her dual role as party chair and primary candidate was a conflict of interest
Tennessee's mid-decade redistricting survived its first legal challenge as a state panel dismissed the NAACP's lawsuit over the map splitting majority-Black Memphis across three districts
North Carolina lawmakers advanced bills to cut early in-person voting from 17 days to as few as 10 and eliminate a Sunday voting day statewide

Wisconsin's League of Women Voters sued to require all municipal clerks to notify voters about absentee ballot certificate defects and allow corrections, challenging the current inconsistent patchwork practice
